title: Cross-border compliance intake and prioritization playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Scope: Define a concise intake and prioritization playbook specifically for enterprise customer asks that involve cross-border data flows, data sovereignty / residency concerns, and multi-jurisdictional compliance checklists (GDPR/DPA, SOC2/ISO, HIPAA). Deliver a lightweight decision matrix, SLA guidance by risk tier, an LLM-assisted summary template for rapid assessor review, and an evidence-bundling checklist to accelerate response times.

Goals: 1) Reduce average time-to-triage for cross-border security/compliance asks from current ~10 business days to <= 3 business days for low/medium risk; 2) Provide deterministic routing to Legal, Privacy, Security, and Regional Ops with clear SLAs; 3) Automate initial classification and evidence-suggestion using an LLM summarizer prototype; 4) Produce a playbook and ship a minimal Console UI that surfaces intake score, recommended owner, and SLA tier.

Out of scope: Full vendor contract negotiation, legal sign-off for exceptions, and custom engineering changes to customer infra. Those will remain escalations after triage.

Deliverables: playbook doc, decision matrix CSV, Confluence intake form template, Console mock for intake score card, prototype LLM summarizer PR, acceptance tests and rollout runbook.
acceptance_criteria: Playbook published in Confluence with sign-off from Legal, Privacy, Security leads
Console intake card mock wired to intake pipeline in staging
Automated classifier achieves >=75% agreement vs. manual triage on a 200-ticket holdout
SLA definitions and escalation contacts documented and added to on-call rota
Evidence-bundling checklist reduces follow-ups by >=40% in pilot accounts
comments: 2025-01-15 - Initial scoping: Product kickoff with Legal (Elena Garcia), Privacy (Suresh Rao), and Security (Priya Menon). Alignment on three risk tiers: Low (info-only), Medium (requires Data Processing Addendum), High (requires legal review + dedicated onboarding).

2025-01-20 - Decision: Use a lightweight scoring rubric (data types + residency + contractual ask + tech exposure) to compute an intake score. Marcus to prototype score calculation; ENG to advise on data needed from intake form.

2025-01-24 - Design review: DES reviewed proposed Console card. Feedback: show 'Most likely owner' and 'Evidence checklist' collapsed by default, include a copyable summary for outbound emails. Action: DES to deliver 2 variants for A/B test.

2025-01-28 - Engineering sync: ENG flagged that PIIs in intake text should be redacted before model summarization. Agreement: redaction run in preprocessor; LLM gets tokenized minimal context. ENG issue created ENG-4820 for preprocessor work.

2025-01-30 - Prototype update: LLM summarizer (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/triage-prototypes/pull/18) now returns 3-line summary + suggested evidence keys. Need privacy review for LLM use on customer-submitted questionnaire text.
2025-02-02 - Legal note: Elena Garcia - approved playbook language for DPA/transfer risk tiers, suggested adding an explicit fallback for EEA->APAC transfers. Updated decision matrix accordingly.

2025-02-02 - PM checklist: created Confluence draft (https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/COM/Cross-border+Intake+Playbook). Link shared with stakeholders for comment. Next: schedule pilot with 3 existing enterprise accounts for Feb 17.
2025-02-03 - Risk: Outstanding item - SLAs for private deployments (on-prem/VPC) still need engineering input to estimate remediation lead times. Marcus to align with infra leads by Feb 10.
next_steps: Finalize scoring rubric and publish CSV template
Complete redaction preprocessor (ENG-4820) and test on 200 anonymized tickets
Run a closed pilot with 3 enterprise customers (legal-signed NDA) to validate SLA and evidence checklist
Design to deliver Console card variants for A/B test by Feb 14
Rollout communication plan for Customer Success and Solutions Engineering
notes: Rationale: growing number of requests mention unique residency clauses and non-standard DPAs. Current manual routing creates 7-12 day delays and inconsistent prioritization.
Automation guardrails: any LLM-based classifier or summarizer must tag outputs as "suggested" and never auto-approve legal decisions.
Fallback policy: if automatic triage score == High, immediately create ticket for Legal and assign provisional SLA of 10 business days until triage complete.
